answer_1.quote: Given the claim, the accurate premise, and the publication contexts, the model must verbalize the fallacious reasoning and assign fallacy classes... We evaluate the reasoning abilities of two state‑of‑the‑art LLMs in reconstructing the fallacious reasoning on MISSCI.
answer_1.outputs: Generated fallacious premises together with predicted fallacy class labels

answer_2.quote: We then report METEOR score, BERTScore, NLI‑A, NLI‑S as automatic evaluation metrics, as well as P@1, Arg@1 and micro F1 for fallacy classification performance.

answer_3.quote: We measure the LLM's internal consistency of the generated premise and fallacy class, by prompting the same LLM again to classify the fallacy present in the generated fallacious premise.

answer_4.quote: We manually evaluated 240 predictions from the main experiments... For each prediction we answered Q1–Q4 to assess premise plausibility, reasoning‑gap coverage, fallacy‑class match, and whether the same reasoning flaw is expressed.
answer_4.guideline: Four manual questions (Q1–Q4) assessing: (Q1) whether a fallacious premise was generated, (Q2) whether it bridges the reasoning gap, (Q3) whether the predicted fallacy class matches the premise, and (Q4) whether it expresses the same reasoning as the reference.
